evidence.exact_quote: Storage for the rewrite follows a multi-store design: **seglog** as the canonical append-only event stream, **redb** for durable KV state (settings, sessions, runs, checkpoints, editor state, analytics rollups), and **Tantivy** for full-text search.
redb projections, JSONL mirror files, and Tantivy indices are rebuildable from seglog plus stable checkpoints; none of them outrank seglog as authority

items.impact: The authority hierarchy and rebuild direction are explicit, preventing mirrors and indexes from silently becoming competing sources of truth.
items.statement: Seglog is the canonical event authority, while redb, JSONL, Tantivy, and analytics state are derived or rebuildable consumers.
items.title: Multi-store authority and rebuild direction are explicit

evidence.exact_quote: PM parses `.gitmodules`/gitmodules, separately bare-clones each submodule repo after validating submodule paths, stores them under `git/modules/{submodule_path}/`, and includes `/modules/{submodule_path}/` content by reading the gitlink-referenced commit via `git show`.

items.impact: A hostile or malformed submodule declaration could select an unintended host, protocol, credential route, or recursive graph even when its local path passes validation.
items.statement: The remote submodule contract requires path validation but does not define validation of submodule URLs, protocols, host allowlists, credential forwarding, recursion cycles, or failure isolation.
items.title: Remote submodule trust boundary is only partially specified

evidence.exact_quote: compression: "none" | "lz4"
readers validate `payload_length`, then checksum, then decode.

items.impact: A valid compressed record can force excessive memory or CPU during replay, block recovery, and turn a durable event log into a denial-of-service vector.
items.statement: The LZ4 wire contract has no uncompressed-length field, maximum expansion ratio, decode budget, or deterministic over-limit recovery behavior.
items.title: LZ4 decoding is not resource bounded

evidence.exact_quote: the corrupt record is skipped
readers validate `payload_length`, then checksum, then decode.

items.impact: If the length prefix itself is corrupt, a reader cannot know the next record boundary, so 'skip' is not implementable and replay can loop, discard valid suffix records, or diverge across implementations.
items.statement: CRC failure behavior names a skipped record but does not specify frame resynchronization, segment quarantine, sequence-gap representation, or when the corrupt suffix is truncated.
items.title: Corrupt seglog framing has no deterministic resynchronization rule

evidence.exact_quote: When two distinct n-grams produce the same xxh3 64-bit hash, their posting lists are merged at index time (Roaring union); the lookup table has exactly one entry per unique hash. Collisions broaden candidates but never affect correctness.
Postings store `u32` file IDs only; line-level precision always comes from ripgrep verification on candidate files.

items.impact: Hash collisions may cost performance but cannot create false search results because authoritative content verification remains mandatory.
items.statement: The sparse-index collision behavior deliberately broadens candidates and preserves correctness through ripgrep verification.
items.title: Index hash collisions have a defined correctness backstop

evidence.exact_quote: a persisted value family is implementation-authoritative only when the registry row identifies its key shape, value schema id/ref, owner doc, producer, consumers, schema version, encoding, required/optional/nullability fields, replay behavior, migration rule, retention/compaction rule, redaction/no-secret rule, and legacy/canonical crosswalk status.
`buildability_gate_passed` remains false.

items.impact: Prose-only families cannot be mistaken for implementation-ready schemas, and the section does not overclaim buildability.
items.statement: The value registry is named as machine authority and incomplete families are explicitly deferred rather than silently promoted.
items.title: Registry authority and partial-closure limits are explicit

evidence.exact_quote: Writers provide an idempotency key plus expected `agent_revision` or `last_applied_event_id`; the append and projection result are one logical append/CAS boundary.
The projector advances `coordination_*_projection.v1` rows and `projector.checkpoint.coordination:{project_id}` in one redb transaction.

items.impact: A crash after seglog append but before redb projection or response can make the caller retry against stale revision, observe a conflict, or receive a result that does not identify the already-committed event.
items.statement: The text calls seglog append plus redb projection one logical CAS boundary but defines transactionality only inside redb; it does not define the durable crash-reconciliation protocol across the two stores.
items.title: Coordination append and CAS lack a cross-store recovery contract

evidence.exact_quote: Canonical records are immutable once committed; corrections require a new record with explicit lineage.
All canonical records include `created_at_utc`, `updated_at_utc`, and `created_by` for audit.

items.impact: Implementers can either mutate `updated_at_utc`, violating immutability, or leave it equal to creation time, making the required field semantically misleading.
items.statement: The baseline simultaneously requires immutable canonical records and an `updated_at_utc` field without defining whether that field belongs to the original record, a successor correction, or a mutable projection.
items.title: Immutable-record update timestamp semantics are unresolved

evidence.exact_quote: Stored bulk outcomes preserve target preview reference, scope summary/count (`/count`), result state, `partial-success`, `per-target` failure list, spawned attempt/remediation refs, and rollback/undo expectations where possible.

items.impact: Destructive multi-target operations can report partial success without a deterministic compensation state, retry boundary, or user-visible distinction between reversible and irreversible targets.
items.statement: The bulk-action record makes rollback and undo expectations conditional on 'where possible' but does not require per-target reversibility, compensation status, or a terminal recovery oracle.
items.title: Bulk partial-success recovery is not deterministic

evidence.exact_quote: Logout, unlink, and project-delete cleanup invalidates non-secret residue such as validation snapshots, last-used account identity, workflow admin receipts, registry capability snapshots, kube context selections, discovered endpoints, and downloaded scrubbed artifacts.

items.impact: A crash or disk failure during unlink or deletion can leave account and endpoint metadata behind without a durable indication that cleanup is incomplete or should resume.
items.statement: Sensitive-residue invalidation names the data to remove but omits cleanup ordering, tombstone state, retry/idempotency rules, failure receipts, and a completion oracle.
items.title: Logout and project-delete residue cleanup is not crash recoverable

evidence.exact_quote: Concurrent mutable control of the same `project_id`, `repo_id`, `/workspace-root`, `/repo/runtime`, runtime target, or hosted `remote_repo_ref` is unsupported unless a canonical project/target lock exists.
If another owner is detected, the affected surface degrades to read-only or explicit override mode; receipts record the cross-process ownership conflict as blocked, not failed.

items.impact: Two instances can both believe they have mutation authority after override, producing split-brain writes and receipts against the same target.
items.statement: The cross-process policy allows an explicit override but does not define who may override, whether the existing owner is fenced, or how stale locks and leases are adjudicated.
items.title: Cross-process override mode lacks fencing authority

evidence.exact_quote: write-capable actions must bind to the same project, host, repo/worktree, and recover-unsaved context that owns the buffer
`cmd.file.delete { project_id, paths: string[] }`

items.impact: After restart, rebinding, or a multi-repo/worktree switch, the stored delete intent can resolve the same path string against a different host or worktree.
items.statement: The text requires write authority to bind project, host, repo, worktree, and unsaved context, but durable `cmd.file.*` payloads carry only `project_id` and path-oriented fields.
items.title: File mutation receipts omit required host/repo/worktree identity

evidence.exact_quote: `repo_id` is stable per project repo root and derived from canonical VCS root identity using a `vcs_root_fingerprint`, with candidate format `gitrepo::<project_id>::<vcs_root_fingerprint>`.

`worktree_id` is stable per concrete worktree instance and derived from canonical realpath identity using `worktree_realpath_fingerprint`, with candidate format `worktree::<repo_id>::<worktree_realpath_fingerprint>`.

items.impact: Different implementations can mint different IDs for symlinked, case-folded, moved, remote, or recreated repositories and worktrees, breaking receipts, tombstones, and deep links.
items.statement: Repo and worktree identity depend on undefined fingerprint algorithms and are still presented with candidate formats rather than an exact canonical derivation and collision/migration rule.
items.title: Repo and worktree ID derivation remains provisional

evidence.exact_quote: required_approvals: u32,
current_approvals: u32,
auto_merge: bool,

items.impact: A counter can be incremented or replayed without proving distinct authorized approvers, revocation, scope, or policy version, allowing an invalid auto-merge transition.
items.statement: The bundle review gate stores only approval counts and an auto-merge flag; it has no approval identities, authority snapshots, deduplication key, revocation state, or transition oracle.
items.title: Bundle auto-merge is backed by unauthenticated approval counters

evidence.exact_quote: Project roots can be `active`, `missing_on_disk`, `archived_from_ui`, or `deleted_from_registry`; missing roots show `not-found` with `rebind_required` instead of silently matching a same-name path.
`/recreate` creates a new identity, and resumable state is allowed only when the original root/worktree identity is validated.

items.impact: Historical receipts and navigation cannot silently gain authority over an unrelated replacement path.
items.statement: Missing or recreated project/worktree roots preserve tombstone truth and require identity validation before resume.
items.title: Project and worktree tombstones prevent same-name rebinding

evidence.exact_quote: custom_headers: Record<string, string>,
localStorage_persistence: "isolated" | "save_on_close",

items.impact: Authorization headers, API keys, session material, or sensitive web storage can enter redb despite the document's no-secret storage rule.
items.statement: Browser profile persistence accepts arbitrary custom header values and persisted localStorage without excluding secret-bearing names/values or routing them to credential custody.
items.title: Browser profile schema can persist raw credentials

evidence.exact_quote: Required canonical record and projection families include:
`terminal_workspace_state.v1:{project_id}:{workspace_tab_id}`
Storage-plan is the canonical source for terminal persistence keys.
`terminal_layout.v1:{project_id}` — terminal panel layout

items.impact: Implementers can choose incompatible write keys and restore models, fragmenting terminal identity, migration, cleanup, and cross-surface joins.
items.statement: The document first names workspace/section/tab/pane/session records as required canonical families, then later declares a different session/layout/history/profile/env/cwd/scroll/font/color decomposition as the canonical key set without a translation or supersession rule.
items.title: Terminal persistence has two competing canonical key decompositions

evidence.exact_quote: `terminal_history.v1:{terminal_session_id}` — command history
`terminal_env.v1:{project_id}` — environment variable overrides
Transcript chunks are bounded, append-oriented, and referenced by session and scrollback anchors

items.impact: Commands, output, cwd values, and environment overrides can contain tokens or private paths and may be indexed, exported, restored, or retained without a deterministic scrub and deletion policy.
items.statement: Terminal command history, transcript chunks, scrollback, environment overrides, and cwd snapshots are durable families, but their secret classification, redaction-before-persist/index, encryption, retention defaults, and export policy are not specified here.
items.title: Terminal persistence lacks a sensitive-data lifecycle contract

evidence.exact_quote: Storage owns `lock-path` derivation. The active `pm.lock` path is `root-derived`: compute it from the selected `logical-root` and, when the selected durable root is not safe for writes, from the safe-local `fallback-derived` durable-store path while preserving the logical root in lineage and diagnostics.
The active durable-store lock is keyed by `(storage_root, authority_scope, store_family)`.

items.impact: Equivalent roots can derive different locks, and a crashed owner can leave either indefinite read-only behavior or an unsafe takeover with no fencing token.
items.statement: Lock identity and path ownership are named, but canonical root normalization, symlink/case handling, acquisition atomicity, owner metadata, lease/heartbeat, stale-lock recovery, fencing token, and fallback-root equivalence are absent.
items.title: Durable-store lock identity lacks an executable fencing protocol

evidence.exact_quote: Replacement writes for state files, manifests, checkpoints, segment rewrites, or similar durable storage artifacts MUST create `<target>.tmp.<random>` in the target directory, write the full replacement payload there, `fsync` the temp file, and then rename/promote it into place.

items.impact: A crash after rename but before directory metadata is durable can lose the promoted filename on filesystems that require directory sync; platform replacement behavior can also diverge when the target exists.
items.statement: The atomic rewrite recipe syncs the temporary file but does not require syncing the containing directory after promotion or define Windows replace-existing semantics and recovery of an ambiguous promotion result.
items.title: Atomic promotion omits directory durability and platform replacement semantics

evidence.exact_quote: every persistent `/long-lived` storage-managed collection either declares a time-to-live, declares a maximum retained item count, or declares both.
Default TTL is inherited from the owning event family retention window; cleanup is triggered by janitor sweep and segment compaction, with legal-hold or preserved-run anchors opting out explicitly.

items.impact: Builders cannot prove memory/disk bounds or overload behavior, and legal-hold opt-outs can turn nominally bounded collections into unbounded stores.
items.statement: The universal bounded-collection rule requires a TTL or cardinality, but the listed collections mostly name qualitative bound sources rather than numeric defaults, configuration ranges, overflow behavior, or testable janitor deadlines.
items.title: Bounded-collection canon lacks executable numeric bounds

evidence.exact_quote: For each event, update only the projections that own it (JSONL mirror, Tantivy, redb snapshot/projector state, analytics enqueue, etc.).
Commit the new checkpoint only after the owned projection writes are durable.
checkpoints encode enough information to resume without duplicate semantic writes

items.impact: A crash after one sink is durable but before the checkpoint forces replay; without per-sink idempotency, JSONL lines, analytics enqueue, or other effects can duplicate even while another sink is correct.
items.statement: The projector spans redb, JSONL, Tantivy, and analytics but does not define event-id idempotency, sink commit markers, replay deduplication, or recovery ordering needed to satisfy its no-duplicate semantic-write guarantee.
items.title: Multi-sink projector cannot yet prove exactly-once semantic effects

segments.summary: Reviewed the complete storage architecture, identity, regex-index, remote-cache, binary-format, seglog wire, replay, EventRecord, security, migration, failure, concurrency, and acceptance-oracle content. Authority and collision correctness are explicit; adversarial review found unresolved remote-submodule trust, compressed-payload bounds, and corrupt-frame recovery contracts.

Reviewed every registry, coordination, record/projection, receipt, attention, evidence, redaction, privileged-session, freshness, attribution, worktree/lane, migration, temporal, retention, and recovery rule. Partial materialization is honestly bounded; cross-store CAS recovery, immutable update semantics, partial bulk rollback, and sensitive-residue cleanup remain under-specified.

Reviewed every stale-window, scope, panel-state, cross-process mutation, worktree/SCM identity, deep-link, account-switch, retention, provider/runtime family, investigation, blocked projection, GitHub Actions, bundle/note/revision, composer, and audit-event rule. Tombstone behavior is strong; override fencing, destructive file identity, fingerprint canon, and approval authority contain critical negative-space gaps.

Reviewed every preview/browser, artifact/worktree/lane, provider/runtime, projection, terminal, lock/root, atomic rewrite, migration-backup, bounded-collection, mmap/build-concurrency, projector, mirror, rebuild, and checkpoint line. Adversarial review found raw browser-secret persistence, competing terminal key canon, missing terminal privacy lifecycle, incomplete fencing and atomic-promotion durability, non-materialized bounds, and unproven multi-sink idempotency.
